summary: In this GDC talk, Arc System Works technical artist Junior Motomura explains Guilty Gear XRD’s transition from traditional 2D sprites to a cel-shaded 3D look that preserves the series’ anime feel. The talk details the NPR pipeline: tool choices (Unreal Engine 3, Autodesk Softimage), real-time shader previews, and a shader-driven approach that uses vertex colors, thresholds, and reimagined normals to achieve a convincing 2D appearance. Motomura covers outlines and inner-line techniques, two-color texture shading, per-character lighting with no global scene lighting, and a frame-by-frame, limited-animation workflow (roughly 500 bones per character) to retain the iconic 2D appearance in a 3D medium. He frames the ‘X Factor’ as the artist’s intention guiding every step, from modeling to animation, and closes with Q&A on production scale, UV layouts, and future NPR exploration.
title: GDC 2015: Guilty Gear XRD’s NPR Cel-Shaded 3D Art Pipeline
